newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian business confidence rises - survey.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian business confidence rises - survey.

text.p: Australian business confidence surged in the March quarter to its highest level since the December quarter 1994, a survey released on Thursday showed.

The Australian Chamber of Commerce and Industry (ACCI) survey of industrial trends found the number of manufacturers predicting a general business improvement in the next six months rose to 35 percent from 30 percent in the December quarter.
Those expecting a deterioration fell to nine percent in the March quarter from 17 percent previously, it found.
The survey found the outlook for profits was positive, while new orders and output were expected to rise in the June quarter.
"While manufacturing activity in the past three months was below expectations and remained subdued, that largely reflected seasonal factors," ACCI chief executive Mark Paterson said in a statement.
"Significantly, outstanding orders rose, reversing the consistent declines recorded since mid-1995."
The survey found the labour market was still soft with the rate of decline in employment and overtime worked remaining similar to that recorded in the December quarter.
"However, there are tentative signs that labour shedding may abate in the next three months," Paterson said.

The survey also showed a sharp slide in manufacturers' expectations regarding enterprise wage agreements with 19 percent of manufacturers now anticipating lower average wage settlements, compared with 11 percent in the December quarter.
Inflationary pressures remained well under control with falling average selling prices and declining average unit costs in the March quarter.
"Manufacturers expect costs to decline sharply in the next three months with the lowest outcome in the history of the survey," Paterson said.

Export performance of the manufacturing sector was disappointing with the first reported decline since the June quarter 1991, in response to weak export markets and the rising Australian dollar, the survey said.
Capacity utilisation remained low with investment spending on plant and machinery expected to remain steady as a result.
Manufacturers continued to predict declines in capital spending on buildings, the survey found.
